mechanics.mechanic: Open by defining the subject, explaining why it matters in everyday life, and previewing the major questions or applications the discussion will address.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use at the beginning of an educational episode, chapter, or article to orient a broad audience before introducing technical material.
mechanics.avoid: Do not promise more precision, practical utility, or coverage than the piece can deliver.

mechanics.mechanic: Briefly connect the current discussion to a previously covered topic, then mark the boundary between what has already been explained and what will be developed next.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use in serialized content or longer courses where audience understanding depends on cumulative concepts.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid lengthy recaps that delay the new material or assume readers remember details they may have forgotten.

mechanics.mechanic: Present two competing or complementary frameworks, define each in plain language, and show how combining them produces a more complete perspective.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when a topic is commonly framed in only one way and the audience would benefit from a broader decision-making lens.
mechanics.avoid: Do not treat the frameworks as mutually exclusive if they describe different goals or orientations.

mechanics.mechanic: Move from a high-level principle to its underlying biological or causal process, then return to what that process might mean for choices or behavior.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when explaining science-based recommendations so the audience understands both the rationale and the limits of the application.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid presenting a mechanistic explanation as proof that an intervention will produce a specific outcome in every person.

mechanics.function: Correct an intuitive misconception before proceeding
mechanics.mechanic: Identify the interpretation an audience is likely to make, explain why it is incomplete, and replace it with a more precise model before adding further detail.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when terminology carries strong cultural associations or when a simple explanation would lead to misleading conclusions.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid caricaturing the audience’s presumed belief or spending more time on the misconception than on the corrected model.

mechanics.mechanic: Break a broad process into phases, components, or conditions, then explain how the outcome changes across those distinctions.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use for topics in which timing, context, dosage, sequence, or participant characteristics alter the apparent result.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce more categories than the audience needs to understand the central decision or causal relationship.

mechanics.function: Qualify evidence without abandoning the main point
mechanics.mechanic: State what is well supported, separate it from plausible but unresolved interpretations, and identify where evidence is indirect, contested, or context-dependent.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use whenever research findings are heterogeneous, mechanisms are uncertain, or animal and human evidence differ.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid both false certainty and excessive hedging that makes the central conclusion impossible to identify.

mechanics.function: Resolve a seeming contradiction with a conditional summary
mechanics.mechanic: Acknowledge that two observations appear inconsistent, specify the conditions under which each can occur, and conclude with a compact rule that preserves the nuance.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when audiences may encounter apparently conflicting claims or when an answer depends on multiple interacting variables.
mechanics.avoid: Do not collapse a genuinely complex relationship into a slogan that omits the relevant conditions.

mechanics.function: Use callbacks and forward references as navigation
mechanics.mechanic: Return briefly to an earlier principle when it becomes relevant, and signal how the current section prepares the audience for a later application or example.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use in long-form explanations to reinforce retention and make transitions feel logically motivated.
mechanics.avoid: Avoid repetitive reminders, unexplained references to material the audience cannot access, or forward promises that are never fulfilled.
